newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia 97/98 rice output, exports to dip.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia 97/98 rice output, exports to dip.

text.p: Australian (paddy) rice production and exports were forecast to fall slightly in 1997/98 from the record expected in 1996/97 but returns to growers should rise a little, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said.
In its March quarter bulletin, ABARE forecast production of 1.41 million tonnes (paddy) rice in the financial year to end June 1998 from an estimated 1.46 million tonnes in 96/79.
Likewise, exports were forecast to dip to 797,000 tonnes from an expected 820,000 in the current year but average grower returns were seen rising to A$200 a tonne from A$197 a tonne.
"The warm conditions in January and February, the key growing period, have ensured good yields from the record plantings," ABARE said.
"The unprecedented size of the harvest could cause logistical problems with the handling and milling process, which means a longer than usual selling period," the agency added.

ABARE said expectations of increased returns from exports of high quality Australian rice to Japan had not eventuated. "A large proportion of the rice imported under Japan's Uruguay Round minimum access commitments is to be re-exported by Japan as food aid and so is not affecting the Japanese rice market."

Firmer world prices for rice would still see returns to Australian growers rise 1.5 percent in 1997/98, ABARE said, but production was forecast to dip 3.8 percent due to likely restrictions on water quotas.

ABARE said the world supply-demand situation was likely to remain relatively tight for a third year and stocks were set to remain low, so world rice prices were forecast to rise 2.1 percent in 1997/98 to US$387 a tonne.

World production was forecast to rise 1.6 percent in 1997/98 to a record 384 million tonnes from an estimated 378 million in 1996/97, while consumption was seen up 1.9 percent to 384 million tonnes from 376 million this year, ABARE said.
The world trade in rice was forecast to decline by five percent in 1996/97 before rising by 1.1 percent in 1997/98 to 18.3 million tonnes, ABARE said.
